title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-routing-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Alya Chen
description: Motivation: customer fleets running Dedicated reported noisy utilization metrics and poor visibility when priority routed requests caused short-lived bursts; autoscaler decisions were oscillating and operators lacked clear per-priority throughput guarantees. This PR improves burst accounting, adds per-priority throughput guarantees and exposes prioritized utilization metrics for observability. Key changes: 1) introduce a token-bucket based burst controller that is aware of priority classes and decays per-priority tokens independently to avoid cross-priority bleed; 2) surface per-priority in-flight and token utilization metrics to the Console/Prometheus (redwood.dedicated.priority_inflight, redwood.dedicated.priority_token_util); 3) expose a new config on DedicatedFleet spec: throughput_guarantees and burst_policy.priority_weights; 4) autoscaler integration: autoscaler now consults priority token headroom before scaling down to avoid removing capacity serving guaranteed throughput; 5) add end-to-end tests + unit tests for token bucket smoothing and reporting. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-1423) - [x] implementation - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests in perf-canary - [x] Console metrics wired - [x] changelog/release notes prepared; Notes: rolling upgrade required for Dedicated fleets to pick up new config, default behavior remains backward compatible (defaults to previous token bucket global behavior), see release_notes field for operator guidance.

release_notes: Enhancement: Dedicated fleets can now be configured with per-priority throughput guarantees and priority-aware burst controls; operators will see new Prometheus metrics redwood.dedicated.priority_inflight and redwood.dedicated.priority_token_util that enable per-priority utilization dashboards. Default behavior unchanged for existing fleets. Rolling upgrade required to opt into new throughput_guarantees and priority weights.
notes: Backwards compatible default; recommend canary rollout to 10% of fleets then monitor redwood.dedicated.priority_token_util and scale decisions for 48h before full rollout.
changelog: Added priority-aware token bucket burst controller; exposed per-priority utilization metrics; autoscaler now respects priority headroom when considering scale-down; new FleetSpec fields: throughput_guarantees, burst_policy.priority_weights.
